name: DL-COVID-19 (Descartes Labs mobility index)
what_it_holds: Descartes Labs' mobility statistic (m50: median max-distance moved per day by a typical device; m50_index: percent of Feb-Mar 2020 baseline) at US state (admin1) and county (admin2) level with FIPS codes, provided in NDJSON, long-format CSV, and wide-format CSV (dates as columns). Starts 2020-03-24, CC BY 4.0 licensed, 400+ commits with regular releases.
why_useful: An independent, non-SafeGraph, non-Google mobility index at daily county granularity with a clean, well-documented, actively-maintained-looking commit history — useful as a cross-check series against the SafeGraph/Google flow data above, and as another distance-moved proxy for gap #5/#11 travel-shock studies.
size_hint: Daily CSV/NDJSON per state+county, hundreds of rows per day, multi-year
themes: Public-health and mobility indices: Google/Apple mobility archives, Cuebiq, SafeGraph/Advan/Dewey samples, Placer.ai-like foot traffic, mobility datasets by city
why_all: An independent, non-SafeGraph, non-Google mobility index at daily county granularity with a clean, well-documented, actively-maintained-looking commit history — useful as a cross-check series against the SafeGraph/Google flow data above, and as another distance-moved proxy for gap #5/#11 travel-shock studies.

name: COVIDExposureIndices (PlaceIQ Location Exposure/Device Exposure Index)
what_it_holds: PlaceIQ-sourced smartphone movement exposure indices: Location Exposure Index (LEX, cross-geography device co-visitation share) and Device Exposure Index (DEX, commercial-venue co-visitation, with income/education/race-quartile splits), published twice weekly (Wed/Sat) as compressed CSVs at state (51), county (~2,000), and CBSA level, 2020-01-20 through 2021-08-24 (discontinued). Underlies Couture/Dingel/Green/Handbury/Williams, Journal of Urban Economics 2021; IRB-approved (UC Berkeley / U Chicago).
why_useful: A third independent commercial-mobility provider (PlaceIQ, a SafeGraph/Advan/Cuebiq peer) with CBSA-level granularity and demographic splits not present in the Google/Apple/SafeGraph series above — useful for city-level (CBSA) foot-traffic/visitation cross-checks and as a template for how commercial location-data vendors structure exposure/visitation indices, relevant to gap #2 (realized occupancy proxies) and #5/#11.
size_hint: 154 stars, 335 commits; twice-weekly compressed CSVs across the full date range
license: Academic use with citation requirement (Journal of Urban Economics 2021 paper)
themes: Public-health and mobility indices: Google/Apple mobility archives, Cuebiq, SafeGraph/Advan/Dewey samples, Placer.ai-like foot traffic, mobility datasets by city
why_all: A third independent commercial-mobility provider (PlaceIQ, a SafeGraph/Advan/Cuebiq peer) with CBSA-level granularity and demographic splits not present in the Google/Apple/SafeGraph series above — useful for city-level (CBSA) foot-traffic/visitation cross-checks and as a template for how commercial location-data vendors structure exposure/visitation indices, relevant to gap #2 (realized occupancy proxies) and #5/#11.

name: worldbank/OvertureLink-Data-Pipeline
what_it_holds: World Bank-authored (MPL-2.0) ETL pipeline to query/extract Overture Maps data (roads, buildings, and by extension places) into ArcGIS Online, common GIS file formats, or local dumps for repeated use.
why_useful: Institutional-grade, maintained pipeline for pulling Overture POI/building data repeatedly -- useful as tooling for a recurring hotel/lodging-supply count if the team wants a maintained World Bank pipeline instead of a one-off script.
themes: POI and place data: Overture Maps places, OSM extracts (tourism=*), Foursquare open places, Geofabrik tooling; counting STR/hotel supply from maps
why_all: Institutional-grade, maintained pipeline for pulling Overture POI/building data repeatedly -- useful as tooling for a recurring hotel/lodging-supply count if the team wants a maintained World Bank pipeline instead of a one-off script.

name: mikeqfu/pydriosm
what_it_holds: GPL-3.0 Python package (48 stars) for downloading, reading, and PostgreSQL-based I/O of OpenStreetMap data (Geofabrik and BBBike sources), analogous to osmextract but in Python.
why_useful: Python-native alternative to osmextract for the same OSM tourism=* tag extraction workflow, useful if the team's pipeline is Python/DuckDB-based rather than R.

name: gsueur/osm-geoparquet
what_it_holds: Pipeline (10 stars, updated 23 Jul 2026) converting Geofabrik OSM PBFs into state-partitioned, theme-filtered GeoParquet extracts.
why_useful: Converts Geofabrik PBFs into an analysis-ready, queryable columnar format (GeoParquet), which materially lowers the effort of filtering to tourism=hotel/guest_house/apartment tags at scale (e.g. all US states) for a supply-count series.
